harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired bin/merge on node1. It now performs CSV-aware numeric ordering, preserves quoted comma-containing fields, emits one header, collapses identical duplicates, rejects conflicting duplicates with a clear explanation, and publishes atomically so failures preserve merged.csv. The repair persisted across the required node reboot.
actions_performed: Replaced the raw cat|sort implementation with a Python 2.7-compatible merge utility for RHEL 7.
Published the staged east.csv and west.csv exports into merged.csv.
Tested successful merging and conflicting-duplicate failure behavior.
Safely rebooted node1 and re-ran all functional and persistence checks.

evidence.requirement: Numeric ordering, quoted fields, one header, and identical duplicate collapse
evidence.summary: Parsed verification proves IDs are ordered 2, 10, 100; the quoted “Tape, wide” field remains intact; one header is emitted; duplicate ID 2 is collapsed.

evidence.requirement: Conflicting duplicates stop publication and explain the conflict
evidence.summary: Merge exits 1, identifies transaction ID 2 and both conflicting source rows, while before/after merged.csv hashes remain identical.

evidence.requirement: Legacy platform compatibility and unchanged OS/kernel
evidence.summary: Implementation compiles under system Python 2.7; pre- and post-reboot checks show RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 unchanged.

Healthy baseline used boot ID d72bd4ec-4e55-42df-9c71-99b4f4ace0ec; safe reboot was acknowledged; node returned with changed boot ID fdca696c-4b46-4c67-940c-c6d3b0b5f52f; artifact hashes, successful merge behavior, published data, and conflict safety all recovered.
